title: Liam Rosenior hints Chelsea will stop doing pre-game huddle over match ball
content:
Liam Rosenior has hinted Chelsea will stop doing a team huddle over the ball in the centre circle before a game kicks off from now on.

Chelsea have faced scrutiny for doing the ritual ahead of the home game against Newcastle United on Saturday despite referee Paul Tierney being in the middle of it.

They have been doing huddles there before kick-off and occasionally at the beginning of the second half since winning 3-2 at Napoli in January.

While Rosenior has always insisted it was not designed to antagonise opponents, he admits that it has become a negative distraction and Chelsea could now change where the do so, starting with the Champions League second leg against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday night.

“I think in terms of the huddle it has been blown out of proportion to be honest,” Rosenior told his news conference on Monday. “It is a small, small thing among many serious things we need to address such as the massive game against PSG tomorrow.

“The lads have always wanted to show togetherness and unity and they will continue to do that. But what we don’t want to do is antagonise or bring more noise on ourselves. We will make a decision on where we do that on the pitch tomorrow.”

The idea was something the players came up with rather than Rosenior, although player support and development officer Willie Isa was also involved.

Rosenior has still come under criticism for defending the practice after Saturday’s 1-0 defeat to Eddie Howe’s side, saying after the loss that the players were there to “respect the ball” and that he was going to speak to PGMOL, the organisation that manages English football’s leading officials, about what had occurred.

He was upset with Tierney’s role in the incident and also complained that they should have been awarded a penalty for Nick Woltemade’s challenge on Cole Palmer in the area.

Chelsea are looking to overturn a 5-2 aggregate deficit against PSG on Tuesday.
